rule: To distill agentsync outcomes for a project, that project's OWN origin must carry the agentsync coordination branch. distill() reads origin/<agentsync_branch> of CAMBIUM_REPO only — it will not reach a board hosted on a different repo, and released claims are never reconstructed from history.
reason: In balatron's first cycle distill() returned 0 agentsync items and reported 'no coordination branch found', because balatron's origin has no agentsync branch — the team's live board lives on agentsync-remote/aethermoor, and all of balatron's claims had already been released. Cambium silently falls back to context-keeper only, so you lose every agentsync outcome-memory without any error. Verify the branch exists (git ls-remote --heads origin agentsync) before trusting a distill's agentsync count.
triggering_incident: balatron distill on 2026-07-10: sources.agentsync = 'no coordination branch found'; 80/80 items came from context-keeper, 0 from agentsync.

rule: In PR-mode org promotion, promote items to org ONE AT A TIME — merge each cambium promotion PR before opening the next. Do not open multiple org promotion PRs against knowledge.json concurrently.
reason: Each promote(item_id, to_scope='org') branches off origin/main and appends to the same knowledge.json items array. Two concurrently-open promotion PRs edit the same region of that array, so the second cannot merge cleanly until the first lands — this is the documented non-transactional PR-mode limitation. Serializing (open PR, merge, then promote the next) avoids the conflict entirely.
triggering_incident: knowledge PRs #1 (con-016) and #2 (con-014) were opened back-to-back on 2026-07-10; PR #2 required manual conflict resolution against knowledge.json before it could merge.

rule: Roll cambium and agentsync out together. Never let the two repos straddle MCP SDK majors: their branches must land in the same cycle, and the shared Python install must be upgraded once for both.
reason: test_cambium.py imports agentsync_server directly, and distill() imports it at runtime, so cambium executes agentsync's module-level code. If one repo is on SDK v1 code while the installed SDK is v2, that import fails at mcp.server.fastmcp, which no longer exists. The failure surfaces as a ModuleNotFoundError inside cambium's test suite pointing at a file in another repository, which reads like a cambium bug and is not one.
triggering_incident: During the 2026-07-28 migration, cambium's suite was run with agentsync's working tree restored to main (v1 code) while the test venv had mcp 2.0.0 installed. test_real_agentsync_integration and test_real_agentsync_release_capture both failed with ModuleNotFoundError at agentsync_server.py line 69. Re-running with agentsync on its migration branch turned 2 failed / 88 passed into 90 passed, with no code change.

rule: Never track .cambium/knowledge.json in this repo. The local knowledge store must stay gitignored here, because this repo is public and local scope accumulates captures quoting every project the operator works in. Knowledge that should travel goes to team or org scope, which have their own repos and their own gates.
reason: DESIGN calls local scope "yours; not shared", but local scope physically lives in the project repo - so for a PUBLIC project repo those two statements contradict each other, and the contradiction is invisible while the store happens to be empty. It was committed empty (items: [], only distill watermarks) and stayed harmless for months. The first session that captured real cross-project knowledge into it put dozens of references to other projects on the machine - including one with no remote at all - into a file staged for a public push. con-015-12da in context-keeper forbids exactly this and notes the failure is silent, one-way, and cannot be reliably unpublished once pushed. Nothing in the tool, the test suite, or code review flags it; the file simply appears as a normal modified file in git status. Note that the write-up of an incident like this must itself be generic: naming the projects involved would leak, in the explanation, the very thing the rule exists to protect.
triggering_incident: Caught on 2026-08-16 at git-add time, after a session captured two dozen cross-project law items into the local store. The staged diff was inspected for other-project references before committing only because con-015-12da was fresh in context from earlier in the same session; a routine `git add -A` would have published it. Untracked with `git rm --cached` (the file stays on disk) and gitignored alongside pages.json and snapshot.json, which were already excluded for the identical reason. The only loss is three distill watermarks, which re-import harmlessly.

rule: A Cloudflare Worker that gates static assets MUST set `run_worker_first = true` under [assets], and every deploy must verify the gate by requesting a protected path WITHOUT the credential and asserting 404. Never deploy data before the gate has been proven on a data-free build.
reason: Cloudflare serves a matching static asset BEFORE invoking the Worker script unless run_worker_first is set. A Worker whose fetch handler checks a path token therefore never runs for any path that matches an uploaded file, so the auth check is silently absent on exactly the URLs that matter. The failure presents as a completely normal successful deploy: wrangler reports success, the Worker exists, the code is correct, and the credential check is simply never reached. There is no error anywhere.
triggering_incident: 2026-08-16: deployed a token-gated dashboard Worker with [assets] pointing at a bundle containing snapshot.json - 869KB of cross-project memory with entry bodies from 20 projects, several private and one with no remote. The gate code was correct but never executed: https://<worker>.workers.dev/snapshot.json returned the full file to unauthenticated requests. Caught within about four minutes by the post-deploy gate test, which requested protected paths without the token and expected 404. Remediation had to be a deny-all Worker deployed over the same name, because `wrangler delete` left the edge serving the old assets for at least a minute. Worse, a --no-data build flag had been written specifically to prevent this and was used for an earlier Pages attempt, then skipped for the Worker deploy - the safety mechanism existed and was bypassed by the person who built it.

rule: NEVER spend the user's money. No metered API call, no billed CLI invocation (including `claude -p` / headless Claude Code), no paid service, no tokens purchased outside the interactive session the user is already paying for - not to build a feature, not to test one, not to inspect a response shape. If a design needs a paid call, say so and quote the price BEFORE writing the code, and do not present it as an option without its cost attached. Never put a billed call on a timer, a hook, or any unattended path.
reason: Money leaves the user's account and does not come back, and an automated caller can do it repeatedly while nobody is watching. The specific failure was worse than the amount: a step that made a metered model call per item was wired into a scheduler firing every five minutes and shipped switched ON, which is a standing charge disguised as a feature. Cost is also invisible in a way bugs are not - nothing errors, nothing looks wrong, and the only signal is a bill arriving later.
triggering_incident: Building a "send for eval" button, an agent audit step was implemented as `claude -p` invoked from the 5-minute drain. Three billed calls were made: two feature tests and - the indefensible one - a call whose entire purpose was to look at the shape of a JSON response envelope. Roughly $0.29 total, only $0.1442 of it actually recorded, because cost instrumentation was added AFTER the first spend. The user had been asked which trigger to use and picked the headless option from a list that never mentioned it cost money, so the choice was not informed consent; presenting a paid option without its price is the root failure, not the user's answer. Remediation: the runner was DELETED rather than gated, because a flag that can be flipped is not a guarantee. Sending a pair for eval still files a self-contained request; the reading happens in an interactive session that is already paid for.
